questions.q: What does DATEDIFF('day', [Order Date], [Ship Date]) return?
options: The number of days between Order Date and Ship Date
The exact ship date, formatted as a day name
A TRUE/FALSE value for whether the order shipped the same day it was placed
The day of the month Ship Date falls on
questions.explain: DATEDIFF(date_part, start_date, end_date) returns the difference between the two dates measured in the specified part — here, 'day' gives the number of days between them.

options: A real date, three months after Order Date
The number 3, representing three months
The name of the month three months from now
An error, because DATEADD only works with days
questions.explain: DATEADD shifts a date forward (or backward with a negative number) by the given interval — here, three months after Order Date, returned as an actual date.

questions.q: What is the key difference between DATEPART('month', [Order Date]) and DATENAME('month', [Order Date])?
options: DATEPART returns an integer (e.g. 7); DATENAME returns a string (e.g. "July")
They return identical results in every case
DATEPART only works on years, DATENAME only works on months
DATENAME returns an integer and DATEPART returns a string
questions.explain: DATEPART extracts a date component as a number, useful for sorting or math; DATENAME extracts the same component as readable text, useful for labels.

questions.q: If [Order Date] is July 17, 2024, what does DATETRUNC('month', [Order Date]) return?
options: July 1, 2024 — the date rounded down to the start of the month
The number 7, representing July
"July" as a text string
December 31, 2024 — the end of the year
questions.explain: DATETRUNC rounds a date down to the start of the specified period — for 'month', that snaps the date to the 1st of that month, still returned as a real date.

questions.q: What is the difference between TODAY() and NOW() in Tableau?
options: TODAY() returns just the current date; NOW() returns the current date and time
TODAY() returns a string; NOW() returns a number
NOW() only works inside DATEDIFF; TODAY() works everywhere
They are two names for the exact same function
questions.explain: TODAY() returns the current date with no time component, while NOW() includes the current time as well.
